requirement_title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement_text:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297
Type: feature

## Requirement

MessagePack generated code is not decorated with the `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` attribute. Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

Solution requested: "I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too."

Alternatives considered by the author: none; "it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases."

## Acceptance criteria

- All generated code is decorated with `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`.
- No new setting or option is required to get the attribute. ("I do not feel like a setting is needed")
- An opt-out setting would be acceptable but is optional. ("setting would be fine to have too")
- The generated code still compiles on every supported target framework (the attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted). (derived)
- Existing verified generator snapshots are updated to include the attribute. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- b-kurczynski-dl suggests a coverage-tool workaround instead: exclude `obj\\.*\.g\.cs$` in the `dotnet-coverage` settings XML.
- armadavalor offers a PR: add `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` (and possibly `GeneratedCode`) to the types emitted by the templates under `src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/` (formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers), update the verified snapshots, no setting. Asks AArnott whether he would accept it or prefer to point users at coverage-tool configuration. No maintainer reply in the thread.
- Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open.
verdict_reason: verified high finding(s) backed by receipts: requirement-tests-1, logic-edge-1

checked.what: Existing SourceGenerator tests on head: 169/169 passed, 0 failed
Existing SourceGenerator tests on base: 167/167 passed, 0 failed
Receipts/ExcludeFromCoverageEmittedTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (1/1), passes on head (1/1)
Receipts/ExcludeFromCoverageLegacyTargetsTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 2/2 failed
Receipts/ExcludeFromCodeCoverageEdgeCaseTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 2/2 failed
Regeneration: 222/222 generated files verified by 89 passing snapshot tests on head

findings.claim: The attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so it is not emitted when the consuming project targets netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework. Those are common MessagePack targets. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` already exists on both: .NET Framework 4.0+ and netstandard2.0, with AttributeTargets including Class. The derived criterion only allows conditional emission where the attribute does not exist. So the criterion 'All generated code is decorated' is not met for these targets, and generated code there still skews coverage. The README hunk documents this limitation as if it were inherent.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCoverageLegacyTargetsTests.GeneratedCodeIsExcludedFromCoverageOnNetStandardAndNetFramework. The generator runs with parse options defining NETSTANDARD2_0 and then NETFRAMEWORK. The test asserts that every generated formatter, resolver and helper type carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute and that the output compiles. It fails on head because the attribute sits in inactive #if regions.

findings.claim: The same `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard is applied to the resolver, FormatterCache<T>, GetFormatterHelper, enum, union and string-key templates. Netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework consumers therefore get no exclusion on any generated type. The README text added at README.md:1639-1640 states this limitation and steers users away from expecting the attribute on these targets.

receipt_plan.detail: The same ExcludeFromCoverageLegacyTargetsTests theory covers this: the resolver, FormatterCache and GetFormatterHelper are included in the checked set and lack the attribute under NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK. (generated tests: GeneratedCodeIsExcludedFromCoverageOnNetStandardAndNetFramework)

findings.claim: The generator now unconditionally adds `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` to the user's own `partial class` resolver declaration. `ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` has AllowMultiple=false. A user who already put `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on their `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class MyResolver` gets CS0579 ('Duplicate ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute'). That is a likely input, since it is the obvious workaround for this very issue. Code that compiled on base now fails to build. The same applies to `[CompositeResolver] partial class` via CompositeResolverTemplate.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageEdgeCaseTests.UserAppliedExcludeFromCodeCoverageOnResolverStillCompiles. It drives MessagePackGenerator on a resolver already marked [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] and asserts the output compilation has no errors. Expected: passes on base, fails on head with CS0579.

findings.claim: Every emitted attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 (netstandard.dll) and in .NET Framework 4.0+, and it is valid on classes there. So consumers compiling for netstandard2.0 or SDK-style net4x get generated formatters and resolvers with no attribute. 'All generated code is decorated' is not met for exactly the targets that do support the attribute. The guard is also inconsistent: legacy non-SDK net4x projects do not define NETFRAMEWORK and do get the attribute.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageEdgeCaseTests.NetStandard20ConsumerFormatterIsExcludedFromCoverage. It runs the generator with preprocessor symbol NETSTANDARD2_0 and asserts every generated *Formatter type symbol carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. Fails on head.

hunches.claim: The attribute is emitted only under `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. Projects targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, which MessagePack supports and which are common in coverage-sensitive enterprise codebases, get no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on generated code. This only partly meets the requirement that all generated code is decorated. Compilation is safe, but coverage numbers for those targets are still skewed. Compatibility-wise, the generated output now carries preprocessor directives that user projects compile and snapshot.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator snapshot tests with a compilation targeting netstandard2.0 and check whether the generated formatter and resolver types carry ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. The `#if` guard compiles the attribute out, so the type is not decorated. Alternatively, build a netstandard2.0 sample and inspect the attributes by reflection.

hunches.claim:
The TransformUtilities change from `{` to `{
` when the nesting type has constraints alters the whitespace of generated output for every nested or generic-constrained type. This is a layout change not required by the feature. It could be needed so the new `#if` directive starts on its own line, but it is not covered by the requirement and shifts the verified snapshots and users' checked-in generated output.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the snapshot tests for nested generic types with constraints. Diff the base and head outputs and confirm that the only differences are the new attribute lines and the one added newline after `{`.

hunches.claim: Preprocessor directives such as `#if` inside the generated code must start on a fresh line. The new text `#if...` is written immediately after previous output. In FormatterTemplate, StringKeyFormatterTemplate and UnionTemplate the old literal began `\tinternal sealed class` directly after an `EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces` that may end with `{` and no newline when there are no constraints. The new literals start with `#if` without a leading `\r\n`, so correctness depends on the `{\r\n` fix. Namespace emission and the non-nested case should be verified, since a missing newline would produce a compile error in user projects.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a Union formatter and a string-key formatter for (a) a top-level type in the global namespace, (b) a type in a namespace, (c) a nested type with constraints, and (d) a generic nested type without constraints. Compile each output and check that no `#if` lands mid-line.

hunches.claim: The attribute is applied only to top-level generated types (formatters, resolver, nested helper classes). Nesting partial types emitted by EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces and other generated pieces, such as the GeneratedMessagePackResolver attribute or the check-in-generated static helpers, are not decorated, so 'all generated code' is read narrowly. This is a scope-interpretation matter.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun snapshot tests and grep the generated outputs for types lacking ExcludeFromCodeCoverage, such as nesting partial types.

hunches.claim: The tests only check that the attribute text appears somewhere in each generated file. They never check that the attribute sits directly on the type declaration, and they never check that each generated type (formatter, resolver, FormatterCache, GetFormatterHelper) carries it. Deleting the attribute from the nested FormatterCache or GetFormatterHelper types leaves the resolver file with the attribute on the outer class, so the test still passes. The first test only needs `Contains` per file, and the second only compares counts.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.tt:28 delete-statement: remove the #if/[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]/#endif block before `private static class FormatterCache<T>` -> block deleted; expected to survive because the resolver file still contains the attribute on the outer partial class, so Contains passes and the guarded count equals the attribute count.

hunches.claim: The tests never compile the generated output for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework. They only do string matching on the guard. If the `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` condition were negated or weakened, the guard text would still match and the tests would still pass. No test checks that the attribute is absent when those symbols are defined. The compilation is also never built with those preprocessor symbols.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/FormatterTemplate.tt:14 negate-condition: `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` -> `#if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK` in one template; expected to survive because the test only checks that the guard string appears, and the string `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 ...` is hardcoded in the test, so the mutant would only fail if the test normalized to a different form. The snapshot tests would catch the text change, but this new test would not.

hunches.claim: The `TransformUtilities.EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces` change (`{` becomes `{\r\n` when constraints are present) has no targeted test. The new tests use only non-generic, non-nested types with no constraints. The new attribute test therefore never reaches the `anyConstraints` branch. Reverting the line would only be noticed through snapshot regeneration, if some snapshot has a constrained nesting type.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/TransformUtilities.cs:58 delete-statement: `anyConstraints ? "{\r\n" : ...` -> `anyConstraints ? "{" : ...`; expected to survive in CodeCoverageExclusionTests because it has no generic nesting type with constraints.

hunches.claim: The test source does not cover generic types, nested types, or a multi-resolver (CompositeResolver) case. CompositeResolverTemplate is changed but never exercised by the new tests, since only `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver]` is used. Removing the attribute from CompositeResolverTemplate would go unnoticed by these tests.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/CompositeResolverTemplate.tt:7 delete-statement: remove the attribute block before `partial class`; expected to survive because TestSource has no composite resolver attribute and so never generates that template.

hunches.claim: The README says the attribute is not emitted for netstandard2.0/.NET Framework, but ExcludeFromCodeCoverage exists in netstandard2.0 with .NET Standard 2.0 API surface (System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available in netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+). The guard likely drops the attribute needlessly, so 'all generated code' is not decorated for those targets and the requirement is only partly met. Also, NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK symbols are defined only for the consuming project's TFM, and the README does not document the exclusion rationale.

receipt_plan.detail: Check docs for ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute applicability: it is in netstandard2.0 (mscorlib/System.Diagnostics). Compile a netstandard2.0 consumer with [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to confirm it builds, which would show the #if guard is unnecessary.

The existing source generator tests ran on head: 169 of 169 passed, 0 failed. 9 unverified hunch(es) remain without an executed receipt. 5 thing(s) were not checked, including mutation testing; compatibility byte diff (base vs head serialized bytes); A/B review branches. By signing off, the signer accepts any defect that only those unchecked paths would have revealed. The change is blocked; signing off is not offered until the blocker is fixed.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditional, no setting. Every generated formatter (int-key, string-key, enum, union), the resolver class and its nested FormatterCache/GetFormatterHelper classes always get [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]. The templates are edited directly and no option is added.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Default-on with an opt-out setting, which the requirement says 'would be fine to have too'. Add a boolean generator option, e.g. an `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` property on the formatter/generator options, read from analyzer config such as `build_property.MessagePackExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, defaulting to true. Thread it into each template's model and wrap the emitted attribute line in `<# if (Options.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage) { #> ... <# } #>` in FormatterTemplate, StringKeyFormatterTemplate, EnumTemplate, UnionTemplate, ResolverTemplate and CompositeResolverTemplate. Add a test that setting it to false omits the attribute.
